subject: Notice of Vendor Chain Change and DPA items - Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Rachel Barnes <rachel.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com, ops-security@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Subprocessor chain update + DPA redline summary

Hi Tessa,

Hope you’re well — quick notice from our procurement and security teams: Acme Analytics is onboarding a managed data-labeling partner (BrightLabel Inc.) that will touch de-identified training artifacts for a subset of non-production workflows.

Attached: Acme_Subprocessor_List_v2.xlsx (list + SOC overview) and DPA_Changes_Summary.pdf (we highlighted the requested flow-down language, including the standard 5.2.3 subprocessors clause and a shorter audit-access paragraph).

Can you confirm whether Redwood requires formal written consent for this type of subprocessor (per our MSA), or whether the notice + thirty-day cure window in clause 8.4 is sufficient? We’re also attaching a proposed timeline — they’d like to go live 2026-09-15.

If there are any forms or evidence we should provide (SOC2 report, subprocessor MSA), please let us know and we’ll upload them to the folder linked below.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Barnes
Senior Contracts Manager, Acme Analytics
rachel.barnes@acme-analytics.com
Attachments: Acme_Subprocessor_List_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), DPA_Changes_Summary.pdf (summary)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Barnes <rachel.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: Subprocessor chain update + DPA redline summary

Thanks Rachel — got it and appreciate the heads up. I’ve attached a short checklist for onboarding subprocessors to speed things up on our side.\n
Quick notes:
- We generally accept vendor notices for downstream subcontractors when the vendor provides evidence (SOC2 Type II or equivalent) and agrees to our baseline flow-down language.
- Clause 5.2.3 in Acme’s summary expands our standard audit-access and encryption obligations; that’s the main item I want Legal to confirm.
- Timeline: 48–72 hours for an initial legal/security triage, then we can route to contracting for signoff.

I’m looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (contracts) — Karthik, can you confirm from a compliance perspective whether BrightLabel’s onboarding requires a signed subproc consent, or whether the notice + evidence is enough? I’ve put the Acme attachments in the shared drive link (see thread metadata).

If it helps, request a 7-day extension to the go-live while we complete triage.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: Subprocessor chain update + DPA redline summary

On Wed, Sep 1, 2026 at 11:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — got it and appreciate the heads up.

Triage complete (initial legal/security read):
- Reviewed Acme_Subprocessor_List_v2.xlsx and DPA_Changes_Summary.pdf. BrightLabel has an SOC2 report and a limited-scope BAA for data handling. Good baseline.
- Redlines attached: redwood_redlines_msa_orderform_20260901.docx — summary below.

Summary of redline recommendations (high-level):
1) Acceptable: notice + evidence for standard subprocessors that do not receive customer PII. We can accept the notice path for non-production labeling if BrightLabel’s SOC2 and encryption controls are confirmed.
2) Exception required: Acme’s proposed language in clause 5.2.3 (broad audit rights and unlimited subcontractor chaining) is broader than Redwood policy. We propose the alternative clause in proposed_clause_5_2_3_alternative.txt (limits to reasonable audit scope, 30-day remediation, audit to be performed by an independent auditor or mutually agreed third party).
3) Logging & data retention: Require confirmation of data segregation and retention schedule consistent with the Order Form (we flagged a retention mismatch in the DPA summary).

Action items: 
- Laura: please prepare an Order Form addendum with the alternative clause and incremental assurance language (we will push to Acme for countersignature).
- Neha (Security): confirm BrightLabel’s certs match what was provided and confirm the encryption-at-rest keys and access controls.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_redlines_msa_orderform_20260901.docx, proposed_clause_5_2_3_alternative.txt
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Barnes <rachel.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: Subprocessor chain update + DPA redline summary

Rachel — thanks for sharing the materials and for the quick turnaround. We’ve completed triage and have a path forward. For clarity I’m summarizing agreed next steps below.

What Redwood needs before we approve BrightLabel’s onboarding: 
- Confirmation of BrightLabel’s SOC2 Type II report (we’ve validated initial certs but need the latest report).
- Agreement on the alternative clause we proposed (attached). This limits audit scope to reasonable inspections, requires a 30-day remediation window, and constrains deeper audits to mutually agreed third parties.
- A short addendum to the Order Form documenting permitted subprocessor roles and the retention schedule aligned with the Order Form. Laura will circulate the addendum for countersignature.

Proposed timeline: Acme to confirm the SOC2 link and confirm acceptance of the alternative clause by 2026-09-06; Laura will route the addendum to your contracting team for signature via DocuSign after we receive confirmation. If we do not get confirmation by 9/6 we’ll request a temporary go-live hold until controls are validated.

If Acme is comfortable with the alternative clause, please reply-all with approval and we’ll move to DocuSign.

Thanks all — looping Neha for any final security flags.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
References: Drive folder (see related_links), HubSpot HS-987654, DocuSign envelope-7721
